lesson_title: A Dome and a Tent on One Page
hook_text: Fold the page. Left, bent rods tied into a dome. Right, two A's and a ridge pole. Now make each one survive a storm on paper.
clip_script: Three families. Dome: bent rods tied to hoops, every stick pushed along its length, none bent, strong from any side, like the hoop tent and the beehive hut. Ridge: two A ends and a pole, flat sheets, guy ropes, low walls. Box: poles and a pitched roof, roomy, heavy, and every rectangle needs a diagonal or it folds. Sketch two that differ. Sizes: 21 square metres, 1.8 metres high. Cover on with eyelets, floor turned up. Now the safety list, drawn and labelled: door away from the wind, hooded vent high, vent low, stove place under the peak on a slab, lamp hook, guy ropes, roof at 30 degrees so water never pools. Tick and cross each idea against the lists. Build both from straws and tissue, push, blow, pour a teaspoon of water. Choose the one that springs back, say why, redraw it clean.
visual_style: Whiteboard page folding; dome arcs and A-frame appearing; labels landing on door, vents, stove, guys; a tick-and-cross table; straw models with push arrows and a water drop.
mood: Inventive and rigorous, ideas earning their place.
pacing: Families, sketch, sizes, labels, table, straws, choice, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch two shelters that differ in structure.
